title: Stability-preserving Lossy Compression for Large-scale Partial Differential Equations
problem: Checkpoint/restart (C/R) strategies are vital for fault tolerance in large-scale PDE simulations, but lossy compression risks instability due to loss of physical invariants (e.g., energy), leading to oscillations and divergence.
motivation: Lossy compression offers scalable checkpoint size reduction, but must preserve numerical stability and physical properties to be practical for long simulations with multiple checkpoint-restart cycles.
method: When saving a checkpoint of a PDE simulation, the method compresses the data using lossy compression—a technique that discards some precision to reduce file size—while actively controlling how much kinetic and potential energy are allowed to change during that compression. By constraining these energy perturbations, the approach prevents the simulation from becoming unstable—avoiding divergence and oscillations—when it restarts from the compressed checkpoint. The technique was validated across diverse PDE configurations on the Frontier supercomputer.
key_novelty: This is the first lossy compression method for PDE checkpointing that explicitly controls physical invariants like energy, ensuring simulations remain stable even across multiple save-and-restart cycles.
contributions: Stability-preserving compression framework for PDE simulations
Explicit kinetic and potential energy perturbation control
Maintenance of numerical stability across restart cycles
Minimal error magnification (relative L2 ~2e-6) across cycles
Evaluation on Frontier supercomputer at scale
limitations: Evaluation limited to PDE workloads; generalization to other simulation types unclear; energy-preserving approach may not suit all physics; production deployment details not provided.
